title: Passage and Summit
premise: Petra Reyes, a mountain guide blacklisted after a disaster he may or may not have caused, is hired off the books to find a missing scientific expedition on the Río Sombra. Following the river upstream, he discovers the team alive but captive of a river community led by Ines Calloway, who believes the scientists came to seize the valley's water for a dam consortium — the same consortium that destroyed Petra's reputation years ago. As the dry season drains the river and old loyalties fracture, Petra must choose between delivering the survivors to justice as his contract demands or exposing the truth that would clear his name at the cost of the valley. He chooses the valley, testifying against the consortium in exchange for his own exile made permanent, and ends the book guiding one last party upriver — this time openly, with Ines beside him.
about_author: Kestrel Marchetti is the pen name of a former river guide who spent a decade running commercial trips through three continents before turning to writing full-time. Their fiction draws on real expedition logs and the quiet moral compromises of people who live by maps.

chapters.title: The Last Contract
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Broke and blacklisted, Petra takes an illegal retrieval job from a fixer named Ochoa: locate the Halvorsen expedition, silent for six weeks on the Río Sombra. The emotional beat is reluctant hunger — he needs the money, hates the client, and recognizes the river's name from the worst year of his life.

chapters.title: Miles, Not Years
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Preparing in the border town of Puerto Ladeado, Petra measures his gear, his debts, and his five empty years in distances traveled. A flashback establishes the avalanche that killed two clients and ended his legal career. The beat is grief disguised as competence.

chapters.title: Downstream of Everything
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Petra hires a boatman, Tomás, and begins the ascent, finding the expedition's abandoned lower camp: radios smashed deliberately, not by weather. Someone wanted them unreachable. The beat shifts from routine to dread as Petra realizes this is no rescue — it's an investigation.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Upstream, Ines Calloway watches her river community brace for the dry season while holding the Halvorsen team in the old mission house. She believes they are dam surveyors. Her beat is righteous certainty shadowed by doubt about what her people have become.

chapters.title: The Gorge of Bells
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Tomás refuses to go past the gorge; Petra continues alone on foot, navigating rapids and cliff trails, and finds a survey stake stamped with the consortium's logo — the same company from his past. The beat is vertigo: the mountain he fled has found him again.

chapters.title: Taken
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Petra reaches the mission house and is captured by Ines's sentries before he can speak to anyone. Interrogated separately from the scientists, he realizes both sides assume he's the other's agent. The beat is claustrophobic irony — the rescuer becomes a hostage.

chapters.title: Halvorsen's Ledger
chapters.summary: Dr. Halvorsen's POV. The expedition leader confesses to Petra through the cell wall: half his team were consortium plants, and the real hydrology data proves the dam will drown the valley. His beat is guilt curdling into bargaining — he offers Petra the evidence if he gets them out.

chapters.title: Dry Season Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. With the river dropping daily, Ines must decide whether hostages are witnesses or burdens. A council scene splits her community between mercy and fear. Her beat is the loneliness of command as she realizes keeping the scientists may doom everyone.

chapters.title: Two Kinds of Truth
chapters.summary: Petra and Ines POV alternating. Forced together on a supply run, Petra shows Ines the survey stakes and Halvorsen's partial ledger; she shows him the flooded village downstream that started her war. Neither fully converts the other. The beat is grudging recognition across a shared wound.

chapters.title: The Traitor's Trail
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. One of Halvorsen's planted scientists escapes toward the consortium's forward camp with copied data. Petra tracks him through canyon country, torn between stopping him and letting the truth reach his old enemies. The beat is pursuit as self-interrogation.

chapters.title: Camp Perdida
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Infiltrating the consortium camp, Petra finds his former employer, Marcus Vane, running the operation — and learns Vane engineered the old avalanche cover-up that blacklisted him. Vane offers reinstatement for silence. The beat is temptation wearing a familiar face.

chapters.title: Refusal
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Petra burns the offer, steals the complete hydrology files, and barely escapes downriver as Vane's men open fire. Wounded, he understands the choice is now irreversible. The beat is liberation with a price tag — he has chosen exile over absolution.

chapters.title: Blood in the Shallows
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Vane's mercenaries raid the mission house to erase the witnesses; two villagers die defending it. Ines evacuates the community upriver toward the forbidden source. Her beat is fury hardening into resolve, and the first crack in her hatred of outsiders.

chapters.title: Reunion at the Falls
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Half-dead, Petra reaches Ines's fleeing column and returns the stolen files. Halvorsen confirms the data exonerates the honest scientists and condemns the consortium. The beat is fragile alliance — enemies becoming co-conspirators against a common predator.

chapters.title: The Forbidden Source
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV rotating among Petra, Ines, and Halvorsen. The column climbs into the high basin where the river is born — sacred ground no outsider has seen. Petra documents everything. The beat is awe and trespass braided together; beauty that demands a price.

chapters.title: Vane's Ascent
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Scouts report Vane leading armed men up the only pass, racing the dying river to seize the source and destroy the evidence. Petra proposes a desperate plan: split the column, use the gorge as a trap. The beat is cold clarity — survival now requires strategy, not flight.

chapters.title: The Gorge Stands
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. The trap partially works: Tomás returns with boats to block the river exit, but Halvorsen is killed buying time, and Ines is captured by Vane's rearguard. The beat is victory stained with loss; every gain measured in names.

chapters.title: Summit Bargain
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Petra trades himself to Vane for Ines, then turns the tables: he has already transmitted the hydrology files to journalists and regulators via a satellite beacon hidden since chapter 11. Vane's men, learning their employer is finished, stand down. The beat is checkmate won with truth instead of force.

chapters.title: Justice Outside the Law
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Vane is handed not to police but to the valley's own judgment — exile downriver, stripped of everything, his fate left to the communities he flooded. Ines must decide whether mercy or memory rules. Her beat is the weight of power finally held.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Months later, in a government hearing room, Petra testifies, formally confirming his own blacklist rather than accept a deal requiring silence about the valley. His record stays ruined; the dam dies; the scientists go free. The beat is costly vindication — justice that costs him everything except himself.

chapters.title: Passage
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Petra returns to Puerto Ladeado, repairs his relationship with Tomás, and buries Halvorsen's journal at the source with Ines. The beat is quiet reckoning — measuring life no longer in miles escaped but in miles chosen.

chapters.title: Summit
chapters.summary: Petra and Ines POV closing together. One year on, Petra leads a licensed cultural expedition upriver with Ines as partner-guide, the valley protected by law and vigilance alike. On the summit ridge above the source, they look back down the whole length of the river. The final beat is arrival: the man who measured life in miles finally stands still.
